outputs.exact_statement:
Let $\Lambda\in\mathscr K$ and let $\Pi$ be any countably infinite ICC group. Let $\omega,\nu$ be arbitrary normalized scalar cocycles on them, and let $t,s>0$. Then $$L_\omega(\Lambda)^t\cong L_\nu(\Pi)^s$$ if and only if $t=s$ and there are an isomorphism $\delta:\Lambda\to\Pi$ and a normalized cochain $b:\Lambda\to\mathbb T$ such that $$\label{eq:intro-cochain}
 \omega(g,h)=b(g)b(h)b(gh)^{-1}\nu(\delta(g),\delta(h)).$$ Every specified isomorphism at unit scale has the form $$\theta(u_g)=w\,b(g)v_{\delta(g)}w^*$$ for a unitary $w$ in the target.*

*More explicitly, put $M=L_\omega(\Lambda)$ and $N=L_\nu(\Pi)$, and let $$\theta:pM_n(M)p\longrightarrow qM_m(N)q$$ be a specified isomorphism, where the unnormalized traces of $p$ and $q$ are $t$ and $s$. Then $t=s$, and one may choose $\delta,b$ as above and $z\in M_{m,n}(N)$ so that, for the canonical map $\varphi(u_g)=b(g)v_{\delta(g)}$, $$z^*z=\varphi^{(n)}(p),\qquad zz^*=q,
 \qquad \theta(x)=z\varphi^{(n)}(x)z^*.$$ Whenever such an isomorphism exists, the recovered comparison group $\Pi$ belongs to $\mathscr K$. In particular every factor $L_\omega(\Lambda)$ in this class has trivial fundamental group.

Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, let $\mu$ be any normalized scalar cocycle on $\Gamma$, and let $P$ be a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual. There is a nonzero bifinite $L_\mu(\Gamma)$–$P$ correspondence if and only if $$P\cong L_\omega(\Lambda)^t$$ for a countably infinite ICC group $\Lambda$, a normalized scalar cocycle $\omega$ on $\Lambda$, and $t>0$, for which there are finite-index subgroups $A\leq\Gamma$ and $B\leq\Lambda$, an actual isomorphism $\delta:A\to B$, and a nonzero finite-dimensional projective unitary representation of $A$ with multiplier $$\frac{\mu|_{A\times A}}{\delta^*(\omega|_{B\times B})}.$$ In particular, the reconstructed group $\Lambda$ belongs to $\mathscr K$.

Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, let $\Lambda$ be any countably infinite ICC group, and let $\mu$ and $\omega$ be arbitrary normalized scalar cocycles on these groups.* 1. *Every nonzero bifinite $L_\mu(\Gamma)$–$L_\omega(\Lambda)$ correspondence is a closed bimodule summand of a finite direct sum of the models in Equation [eq:intro-model].* 2. *Every such correspondence has a finite orthogonal decomposition into full-germ orbit bundles. After choosing distinct germ orbits and allowing zero fibres, all bounded bimodule maps are $$\label{eq:intro-hom} \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{M\text{--}N}\!\left(\bigoplus_d H(d,\sigma_d), \bigoplus_d H(d,\tau_d)\right) =\bigoplus_d\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{C_d,\alpha}(\sigma_d,\tau_d).$$ Norm, adjoint, and composition are fibrewise. Projection summands are exactly projective-representation summands in the fibres. A correspondence $K=\bigoplus_d H(d,\sigma_d)$ has dimensions $$\dim_M K=\sum_d\dim_{\mathbb C}(\sigma_d)[\Lambda:B_d],\qquad \dim K_N=\sum_d\dim_{\mathbb C}(\sigma_d)[\Gamma:A_d].$$ Both are positive integers when $K\ne0$.* 3. *Conjugation and Connes fusion correspond to conjugation and balanced tensor product of these bundles. They are equivalently computed by finite double-coset induction. The scalar transports are given explicitly in Equations [eq:input-A1] and [eq:input-A2] and Section 3.

Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, let $\Lambda$ be any countably infinite ICC group, and let $\mu,\omega$ be arbitrary normalized scalar cocycles. Every nonzero separable bifinite $L_\mu(\Gamma)$–$L_\omega(\Lambda)$ correspondence is a closed bimodule summand of a finite direct sum of the models $E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)$ in Equation [eq:intro-model], with the exact multiplier in Equation [eq:intro-multiplier].

The maps $g\mathrel{%
  \pdfliteral direct{/Span << /ActualText <FEFF21A6> >> BDC}%
  \paperoriginalmapsto
  \pdfliteral direct{EMC}}[\mathop{\mathrm{Ad}}(g)]$ and $h\mathrel{%
  \pdfliteral direct{/Span << /ActualText <FEFF21A6> >> BDC}%
  \paperoriginalmapsto
  \pdfliteral direct{EMC}}[\mathop{\mathrm{Ad}}(h)]$ are injective. The group $C_d$ is the graph of an isomorphism $\delta_d:A_d\to B_d$ between finite-index subgroups. It contains $C_\delta$ at finite index, and $\delta_d$ extends $\delta$. If a finite-index subgroup of $C_d$ fixes another germ $x$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Lambda$, then $x=d$. Equivalently, the only finite $C_d$-orbit in the space of these germs is $\{d\}$. The same conclusion holds with $C_d$ replaced by $C_\delta$.

Equation [eq:input-A1] defines a unitary projective representation of $D$ with multiplier $\alpha$. Changing the coset representatives gives a unitarily equivalent bundle by unitary identifications of its individual fibres. If $C$ is the graph of a finite-index subgroup isomorphism $A\to B$, the bundle has commuting normal $M$ and right $N$ actions, and is bifinite.

Let $\delta:A\to B$ be a finite-index subgroup isomorphism and let $\sigma:A\to\mathcal U(V)$ have multiplier $\beta=\mu|_{A\times A}/\delta^*\omega$. Define $\gamma(a,\delta(a))=\sigma(a)$. Then $$E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)=
 L^2(M)\mathbin{\bar\otimes}_{L_{\mu|A}(A)}
       (V\otimes L^2(N))
 \cong\mathcal H(C_\delta,\gamma).$$ The unitary sends the vector $\xi$ in the fibre labelled by $x$ to $U_{r_x}j\xi$, where $j\xi=\widehat1\otimes(\xi\otimes\widehat1)$ in the displayed model.

For a finite-dimensional $\alpha|_{C_d}$-projective representation $\gamma$, $$\label{eq:calculus-full-dimensions}
 \dim_M H(d,\gamma)
   =\dim_{\mathbb C}(\gamma)[\Lambda:B_d],
 \qquad
 \dim H(d,\gamma)_N
   =\dim_{\mathbb C}(\gamma)[\Gamma:A_d].$$ For the original model these formulas read $$\dim_M E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)
   =\dim_{\mathbb C}(\sigma)[\Lambda:B],
 \qquad
 \dim E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)_N
   =\dim_{\mathbb C}(\sigma)[\Gamma:A].$$ Zero fibres may be omitted. Dimensions add under finite orthogonal sums.

Let $M,P$ be $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors and let ${}_M K_P\ne0$ be bifinite. The commutant $Q$ of the right $P$-action is a positive finite amplification of $P$, and the given left action identifies $M$ with a unital finite-index subfactor of $Q$.

Every bifinite $M$–$M$ correspondence has an orthogonal decomposition $$K=\bigoplus_{d\in D}K_d$$ into finite-dimensional spaces, with only countably many nonzero terms, such that $$u_gK_du_h^*=K_{\iota(g)d\iota(h)^{-1}}.$$ The support is contained in finitely many $\iota(\Gamma)$-double cosets. For every representative $\delta:A\to B$ of $d$, $$K_d=\left\{\xi\in K:
  \dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{span}
    \{u_{\delta(a)}\xi u_a^*:a\in A\}<\infty\right\}.
 \label{eq:input-B1}$$ In particular, for the fixed presentation $M=L_\mu(\Gamma)$, the grading is determined by the two actions and does not depend on a choice of arithmetic model decomposition.

Every $K_d$ consists of bounded elements of $Q$, and $$K_dK_f\subset K_{df},\qquad K_d^*=K_{d^{-1}},\qquad
 1\in K_1,\qquad u_a\in K_{\iota(a)}.
 \label{eq:endpoints-grade-product}$$ Consequently $K_1$ is a finite-dimensional unital $*$-subalgebra of $Q$, normalized by the $u_a$, and $\tau_Q(K_d)=0$ for $d\ne1$.

Let $p$ be a minimal projection of $K_1$. There are a countable subgroup $\Lambda\leq D$ and a normalized scalar cocycle $\omega$ such that the actual corner $pQp$, with normalized trace, is isomorphic to $L_\omega(\Lambda)$. Each nonzero space $pK_dp$ is one-dimensional and has a unitary basis vector in the corner.

For the corner in Lemma 16, the group $\Lambda$ is countably infinite and ICC. There are finite-index subgroups $A\leq\Gamma$, $B\leq\Lambda$, an actual group isomorphism $\delta:A\to B$, and a finite-dimensional projective representation with multiplier $\mu|_A/\delta^*(\omega|_B)$.

For composable bifinite correspondences of finite factors, left dimensions multiply under relative tensor product, and so do right dimensions. If $M^t=p(M_n(\mathbb C)\bar\otimes M)p$ and $C_p=pL^2(M)^n$, then ${}_{M^t}C_p{}_M$ is an equivalence correspondence with dimensions $(1/t,t)$ in left/right order.

Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$ and let $\Lambda$ be any countably infinite ICC group. There is a nonzero bifinite $L(\Gamma)$–$L(\Lambda)$ correspondence if and only if $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are abstractly commensurable.

For $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, a separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $P$ is joined to $L(\Gamma)$ by a nonzero bifinite correspondence if and only if $P\cong L_\omega(\Lambda)^t$ for $t>0$, an ICC group $\Lambda$ abstractly commensurable with $\Gamma$, and a finite-type cocycle $\omega$ on $\Lambda$.

For $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, there is an isomorphism of abstract groups $$\operatorname{Out}(L(\Gamma))
 \cong\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Gamma,\mathbb T)\rtimes\operatorname{Out}(\Gamma),
 \qquad [\delta]\cdot\chi=\chi\circ\delta^{-1},$$ where $\operatorname{Out}$ denotes automorphisms modulo inner automorphisms.

Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$ and suppose that $C_r^*(\Gamma)$ has a unique tracial state. If $\Lambda$ is any discrete group and there is a complex-linear $*$-isomorphism $C_r^*(\Gamma)\cong C_r^*(\Lambda)$, then $\Gamma\cong\Lambda$.
An injective homomorphism $\alpha:\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)\to\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$ whose image has finite index is surjective.
Every normal unital complex-linear $*$-endomorphism $\theta$ of $M=L(\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb Z))$ with $[M:\theta(M)]<\infty$ is surjective.
